programme.title: Geamaichean a' Cho-fhlaitheis Glaschu 2026/Commonwealth Games Glasgow 2026
programme.desc: Spòrs beò agus geàrr-chunntasan an latha bho Glaschu 2026. Air a lìbhrigeadh le Derek ‘Pluto’ Moireach agus sgioba aithris BBC ALBA. Live sporting action and highlights from Glasgow 2026. Presented by Derek ‘Pluto’ Murray and BBC ALBA’s commentary team.

programme.title: Na h-Eileanaich: Barra and Vatersay
programme.desc: Barra and Vatersay are often perceived as being just a tourist destination. But a closer look reveals a strong, thriving community not solely dependent on tourism, even without the infrastructure and conveniences of the mainland. This programme shows not only the fragility of a living community but also the determination and robustness of the people within. Thathas tric a’ faicinn Barraigh agus Bhatarsaigh dìreach àite turasachd. Ach, eadhon às aonais bun-structair agus goireasan thìr-mhòir, nuair a choimheadas tu nas mionaidiche, tha coimhearsnachd làidir is soirbheachail ann nach eil a-mhàin steidhichte air turasachd. ’S e program adhartach is sunndach a th’ anns “Na h-Eileanaich” a tha a’ sealltainn, chan e a-mhàin, cho cugalach uaireanan a tha coimhearsnachd bheò, ach cuideachd cho daingeann agus cho neartmhor sa tha a’ choimhearsnachd sin. Le dealbhan àlainn, agallamhan agus guthan-leirigidh, tha sin ga thoirt am follais. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Rudan Beaga Bòidheach/Life’s Little Things
programme.desc: Tha Niamh NicFhionghain a’ coinneachadh daoine òga eile gus rudan beaga fheuchainn a tha a’ toirt toileachas dhaibh. Bho Iòga air mullach cnoc, a bhith a’ sgrìobhadh bàrdachd, gu furachas, dòigh-beatha a’ bhana-campachaidh no a bhith a’ cluich camanachd – tha tòrr ann air an urrainn dhut a bhith taingeil an uair a tha thu air a’ bhlàr a-muigh. Skye digital creator Niamh Mackinnon meets other young people to try out the different little activities that spark joy for them. From hilltop yoga, writing poems, mindfulness, campervan life to playing shinty - there’s so much to appreciate when you just get out there. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Machair
programme.desc: Drama Gàidhlig stèidhichte ann an Leòdhas. Gaelic soap based on the Isle of Lewis.

programme.title: Fraochy Bay
programme.desc: Fàilte gu Fraochy Bay , baile nach fhaic thu a h-uile là! Is iomadh annas a tha ri fhaicinn sa bhaile , agus sin gun ghuth air càil ach muinntir a bhaile fhèin. Tha Là nan Geamannan air a' thighinn agus tha muinntir a bhaile air bhoil. Welcome to the colourful and unusual world of Fraochy Bay, a miniature metropolis somewhere off the fringes of the map. It's time for the Highland games and the residents gather to test their mettle and toss their cabers to see who comes out on top.

programme.title: Alleluia!
programme.desc: Prògram spioradail le laoidhean, sailm agus leughaidhean à Coats ann am Pàislig, air a lìbhrigeadh le Iain MacFhionghain. Am measg na seinneadairean bidh Seumas Greumach, Maeve NichFhionghain, Amy NicAoidh, agus an còisir Binneas fo stiùir John Joe MacNèill. Bidh An t-Urr. Daibhidh MacNeacail a’ meòrachadh air cuspair creideimh le leughadh agus smuain. Cuideachd, dàn is seallaidhean spioradail ann an companachd Dòmhnall Eachann Meek ann an Tiriodh agus bidh Chloe Steele a’ toirt dhuinn seirm adhraidh air a’ phìob à Manachainn nan Lios. Iain MacKinnon presents a mix of hymns, psalms and readings from Coats in Paisley. Among the singers performing are James Graham, Maeve MacKinnon, Amy MacKay, and the choir Binneas, conducted by John Joe MacNeil. The Rev David Nicolson reflects on his beliefs with a selected reading and thought, spiritual poetry and landscapes in the company of Donald E Meek in Tiree and Chloe Steele performs a tune of worship on the pipes from Beauly Priory. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Treasures of Ancient Greece
programme.desc: Alastair Sooke explores the extraordinary afterlife of the Greek masterpieces that changed the course of western culture. Succeeding centuries have found in ancient Greek art inspiration for their own ideals and ambitions. Filming in Italy, Germany, France and Britain, Alastair's investigation includes The Venus of Knidos, the first naked woman in western art, the bronze horses of St Mark's in Venice which became a pawn in an imperial game, and the naked discus thrower, the Discobolus, personally bought by Adolf Hitler and used by him as a symbol of Aryan supremacy.

programme.title: Leonardo
programme.desc: She has her own bodyguards and lives in Paris in a humidified, air-conditioned box protected by triplex bulletproof glass. Despite this, she is visited by six million tourists every year. She is Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa. Alan Yentob tells the story of how the Mona Lisa came to be the most famous work of art in the world. It's a tale full of notoriety, glamour and intrigue as the Mona Lisa is abducted, vandalised and exploited across the centuries. With the help of leading scholars and original research, Alan also finally solves the central mystery of the Mona Lisa - who she is and why she is smiling.

programme.desc: Michael’s rail journey through postwar Scotland takes him over the River Tay to Dundee on the trail of Joseph McKenzie, the father of modern Scottish photography. In Perth, Michael meets a singer-songwriter and veteran of the early Scottish folk scene. At Perth's Wellshill Cemetery, Michael discovers the graves of 355 of the thousands of Polish soldiers, sailors, and airmen who fought for the Allies from British bases. Alighting at Dunkeld, Michael makes for the Loch of the Lowes to spot a magnificent pair of breeding ospreys who nest in the 320-acre nature reserve.

programme.title: Walking With...
programme.desc: Celebrity chef Monica Galetti walks through the open landscapes of the North York Moors. Along the way she meets residents and samples local produce. Starting off with a glorious view over the frost-covered valley, Monica drops down into the historic village of Rosedale Abbey. Following the course of a stream up Rosedale, she climbs towards the heather, passing a fell runner on the way. On top of the moors she experiences the open expanse before her. Getting away from the hustle and bustle of the city gives Monica the chance to reflect and find peace. As her senses tune in to the birdsong around her, she reminisces about her homeland of Samoa and resolves to spend more time out in nature. Crossing over to Farndale, she walks the quiet lanes and enjoys her escape from the heat of the kitchen, before ending with a well-deserved drink in the hamlet of Church Houses.

programme.title: Keeping Up Appearances
programme.desc: When Hyacinth gets passionate about art, Daddy decides to join the Foreign Legion. Meanwhile, Mr Finchley has desires of his own for Rose.

programme.title: One Foot in the Grave
programme.desc: Victor is unable to sleep, and things get so desperate that he contemplates opening Ronnie and Mildred's Christmas present from last year.

programme.title: She-Wolves: England's Early Queens
programme.desc: In the medieval and Tudor world there was no question in people's minds about the order of God's creation - men ruled and women didn't. A king was a warrior who literally fought to win power then battled to keep it. Yet despite everything that stood in their way, a handful of extraordinary women did attempt to rule medieval and Tudor England. In this series, historian Dr Helen Castor explores seven queens who challenged male power, the fierce reactions they provoked and whether the term 'she-wolves' was deserved. In 1308 a 12-year-old girl, Isabella of France, became queen of England when she married the English king. A century later another young French girl, Margaret of Anjou, followed in her footsteps. Both these women were thrust into a violent and dysfunctional England and both felt driven to take control of the kingdom themselves. Isabella would be accused of murder and Margaret of destructive ambition - it was Margaret who Shakespeare named the She Wolf. But as Helen reveals, their self-assertion that would have seemed natural in a man was deemed unnatural, even monstrous in a woman.

programme.title: Castles: Britain's Fortified History
programme.desc: Sam Willis tells the story of the English ruler who left the most indelible mark on the castle - the great Plantagenet king, Edward I, who turned it into an instrument of colonisation. Edward spent vast sums to subdue Wales with a ring of iron comprised of some of the most fearsome fortresses ever built. Castles like Caernarfon and Beaumaris were used to impose England's will on the Welsh. But when Edward turned his attention to Scotland, laying siege to castles with great catapults, things didn't go so well for him.

programme.title: Corridors of Power: Should America Police the World?
programme.desc: In 2003, the Sudanese government began a widespread ethnic cleansing campaign in the western part of the country. With the memory of the genocides in Bosnia and Rwanda still fresh, hundreds of thousands of Americans went out to protest and demand protection for the citizens of Darfur. Despite the US being bogged down in Iraq and Afghanistan, the Bush administration did not stand aside, but couldn’t take the US into another war. Following Obama’s 2008 election success, many of the people that fought so vocally for Darfur came into office. Could they make a difference?

programme.title: Corridors of Power: Should America Police the World?
programme.desc: Barack Obama's first presidential trip abroad was to Cairo. He turned to the younger generation in the Arab world and told them 'you, more than anyone, have the ability to remake this world'. A year and a half later the Arab Spring broke out, but when Muammar Gaddafi declared his intention to go to Benghazi and 'disinfect it, street after street and house after house', Obama faced a dilemma. Should he heed the call to save innocent civilians from a potential massacre?

programme.title: Treasures of Ancient Greece
programme.desc: Alastair Sooke explores the extraordinary afterlife of the Greek masterpieces that changed the course of western culture. Succeeding centuries have found in ancient Greek art inspiration for their own ideals and ambitions. Filming in Italy, Germany, France and Britain, Alastair's investigation includes The Venus of Knidos, the first naked woman in western art, the bronze horses of St Mark's in Venice which became a pawn in an imperial game, and the naked discus thrower, the Discobolus, personally bought by Adolf Hitler and used by him as a symbol of Aryan supremacy.

programme.title: Leonardo
programme.desc: She has her own bodyguards and lives in Paris in a humidified, air-conditioned box protected by triplex bulletproof glass. Despite this, she is visited by six million tourists every year. She is Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa. Alan Yentob tells the story of how the Mona Lisa came to be the most famous work of art in the world. It's a tale full of notoriety, glamour and intrigue as the Mona Lisa is abducted, vandalised and exploited across the centuries. With the help of leading scholars and original research, Alan also finally solves the central mystery of the Mona Lisa - who she is and why she is smiling.

programme.title: Talking Business
programme.desc: Just how long can Iran afford to keep fighting the US? War is expensive, and Iran's economy is facing recession as people struggle with soaring prices, rising unemployment and a weak currency. But with the fighting continuing, are years of international financial sanctions really having the desired impact? Professor Djavad Salehi-Isfahani, a leading expert on Iran's economy, tells us what he found on a recent visit to Tehran, and Mark Wallace, CEO of campaign group United Against a Nuclear Iran, explains the realities of sanctions. Plus, Ben Thompson also hears from Tom Broughton, founder of London glasses brand Cubitts, about how he's taking on the big names in a multi-billion dollar industry.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: A dramatic new chapter begins at Longleat. After more than 50 years, hippos are returning to the park, but with hopes of creating a world-class breeding programme, the pressure is on. The team must race to finish a state-of-the-art hippo house in time while the keepers travel across Europe on a mission to learn everything they can about their precious new arrivals. But bringing together a pod of hippos who’ve never met and mixing them with the park’s sea lions could spell disaster. Elsewhere, Ben witnesses a rare moment as the Cuban crocodiles show a terrifying pack-hunting display, while on the other side of the park, the keepers hope for peace between the park’s battling hyenas after a savage attack. In Lion Country, Caleb uncovers the astonishingly clever tactics of an ageing lioness determined to outwit her pride and stay strong, and there’s heartstopping jeopardy as Megan helps reintroduce giant tortoises to the sunshine. Meanwhile, Hamza’s bird survey uncovers spectacular scenes in the skies above Half Mile Pond.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Many stolen cars end up in illegal garages known as chop shops, where they’re broken up for parts. Each part is sold on the black market, making it a potentially lucrative business for the criminals. Tracker Richard is racing to find a stolen Audi before it’s dismantled. According to the vehicle’s tracker, it’s being stored in a garage in Newport, south Wales. But will Richard get to it in time? At Felixstowe port, stolen vehicle examiner Adam discovers a shipping container crammed full of car parts. Adam’s job is to piece together the parts and identify the stolen vehicles, one by one. Caravans and motorhomes are also being targeted by criminal gangs. But one proud owner gave chase when his motorhome was stolen. Dramatic dashcam footage shows how he closed in on the thief, eventually forcing him to abandon the stolen motorhome at the side of the road and make his getaway on foot.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: After a teenager is found dead in the woods, a pathologist analyses her stab wounds to shed light on the attack. Plus, when remains are found in Scotland, a crack team of experts nail the killer.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A derelict cottage in Dorset has Martin debating whether it’s more viable to demolish and start again rather than refurbish. Dion’s in Yorkshire, where an end terrace has some structural issues, and in west London Owain loves the potential of a lower ground floor flat.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion hosts as the red and blue teams go head-to-head at Carmarthen Antiques and Flea Market in west Wales, with the expert help of Philip Serrell and Charles Hanson. Who will buy the most profitable three items to take to auction? Christina visits the nearby Gwili Steam Railway and finds out how it has been preserved for future generations.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: At Altrincham recycling centre, Jacqui stops three potential money-makers from being crushed. She enlists carpenter Ollie to overhaul a coffee table, but will his bonkers plan including concrete and a traffic cone prove to be a winner? For her own project, Jacqui tries to add a creative touch to a collection of old frames, but will the results be as pretty as a picture?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: North Yorkshire is calling, and Briony May Williams is on the case as she helps a London buyer and her beloved dog Buddy swap city bustle for a country cottage. With a £350,000 budget as well as her human best buddy by her side for support, the trio discover charming homes, towns and villages for this rural getaway. Briony also meets a family living on the edge of the amazing moors, where they now roast their own coffee beans for their thriving cafe.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: A widow needs help to sell her collectibles. JB finds a rare watch that could make a small fortune at auction, and Robin turns to toothpaste to help restore an antique.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: The brainy quiz returns - but this time host Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Gyles Brandreth. As always, contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It’s week 3, and it's time for Reduce, Reuse, Recycle. Presenter Sophie Willan, alongside judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young, takes the fight to fast fashion with three challenges focused on the environment and sustainability. First up, in the Pattern Challenge, it’s another sewing bee first as the sewers are tasked with creating pants from old T-shirts. However, they are not asked to make just one pair - they have to make three. This challenge tests not only their technical skill but also their consistency. Then, Patrick and Esme take a trip to a store of waste destined for landfill to handpick the raw materials for the Transformation Challenge. Finally, the sewers get protesting as they make outfits with an environmental message made to measure their models.

programme.title: Murder 24/7
programme.desc: Detectives hunt the remaining suspects in the murder of Aurman Singh. Financial data and international cooperation lead detectives to two fugitives hiding in plain sight in Austria.

programme.title: Blinded by the Light
programme.desc: Luton, 1987. Javed Khan is a British Pakistani college student in a family with a domineering father. Facing parental pressure and everyday racism, Javed unexpectedly finds his frustrations and ambitions expressed in Bruce Springsteen songs. Inspired by the rock star and a teacher who encourages his own writing, he sets out to fulfill his dreams. Feelgood drama with music, inspired by a true story.

Finally, the sewers get protesting as they make outfits with an environmental message made to measure their models.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: A dramatic new chapter begins at Longleat. After more than 50 years, hippos are returning to the park, but with hopes of creating a world-class breeding programme, the pressure is on. The team must race to finish a state-of-the-art hippo house in time while the keepers travel across Europe on a mission to learn everything they can about their precious new arrivals. But bringing together a pod of hippos who’ve never met and mixing them with the park’s sea lions could spell disaster. Elsewhere, Ben witnesses a rare moment as the Cuban crocodiles show a terrifying pack-hunting display, while on the other side of the park, the keepers hope for peace between the park’s battling hyenas after a savage attack. In Lion Country, Caleb uncovers the astonishingly clever tactics of an ageing lioness determined to outwit her pride and stay strong, and there’s heartstopping jeopardy as Megan helps reintroduce giant tortoises to the sunshine. Meanwhile, Hamza’s bird survey uncovers spectacular scenes in the skies above Half Mile Pond.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Many stolen cars end up in illegal garages known as chop shops, where they’re broken up for parts. Each part is sold on the black market, making it a potentially lucrative business for the criminals. Tracker Richard is racing to find a stolen Audi before it’s dismantled. According to the vehicle’s tracker, it’s being stored in a garage in Newport, south Wales. But will Richard get to it in time? At Felixstowe port, stolen vehicle examiner Adam discovers a shipping container crammed full of car parts. Adam’s job is to piece together the parts and identify the stolen vehicles, one by one. Caravans and motorhomes are also being targeted by criminal gangs. But one proud owner gave chase when his motorhome was stolen. Dramatic dashcam footage shows how he closed in on the thief, eventually forcing him to abandon the stolen motorhome at the side of the road and make his getaway on foot.

But bringing together a pod of hippos who’ve never met and mixing them with the park’s sea lions could spell disaster. Elsewhere, Ben witnesses a rare moment as the Cuban crocodiles show a terrifying pack-hunting display, while on the other side of the park, the keepers hope for peace between the park’s battling hyenas after a savage attack. In Lion Country, Caleb uncovers the astonishingly clever tactics of an ageing lioness determined to outwit her pride and stay strong, and there’s heartstopping jeopardy as Megan helps reintroduce giant tortoises to the sunshine. Meanwhile, Hamza’s bird survey uncovers spectacular scenes in the skies above Half Mile Pond.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Many stolen cars end up in illegal garages known as chop shops, where they’re broken up for parts. Each part is sold on the black market, making it a potentially lucrative business for the criminals. Tracker Richard is racing to find a stolen Audi before it’s dismantled. According to the vehicle’s tracker, it’s being stored in a garage in Newport, south Wales. But will Richard get to it in time? At Felixstowe port, stolen vehicle examiner Adam discovers a shipping container crammed full of car parts. Adam’s job is to piece together the parts and identify the stolen vehicles, one by one. Caravans and motorhomes are also being targeted by criminal gangs. But one proud owner gave chase when his motorhome was stolen. Dramatic dashcam footage shows how he closed in on the thief, eventually forcing him to abandon the stolen motorhome at the side of the road and make his getaway on foot.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: After a teenager is found dead in the woods, a pathologist analyses her stab wounds to shed light on the attack. Plus, when remains are found in Scotland, a crack team of experts nail the killer.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A derelict cottage in Dorset has Martin debating whether it’s more viable to demolish and start again rather than refurbish. Dion’s in Yorkshire, where an end terrace has some structural issues, and in west London Owain loves the potential of a lower ground floor flat.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion hosts as the red and blue teams go head-to-head at Carmarthen Antiques and Flea Market in west Wales, with the expert help of Philip Serrell and Charles Hanson. Who will buy the most profitable three items to take to auction? Christina visits the nearby Gwili Steam Railway and finds out how it has been preserved for future generations.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: At Altrincham recycling centre, Jacqui stops three potential money-makers from being crushed. She enlists carpenter Ollie to overhaul a coffee table, but will his bonkers plan including concrete and a traffic cone prove to be a winner? For her own project, Jacqui tries to add a creative touch to a collection of old frames, but will the results be as pretty as a picture?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: North Yorkshire is calling, and Briony May Williams is on the case as she helps a London buyer and her beloved dog Buddy swap city bustle for a country cottage. With a £350,000 budget as well as her human best buddy by her side for support, the trio discover charming homes, towns and villages for this rural getaway. Briony also meets a family living on the edge of the amazing moors, where they now roast their own coffee beans for their thriving cafe.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It’s week 3, and it's time for Reduce, Reuse, Recycle. Presenter Sophie Willan, alongside judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young, takes the fight to fast fashion with three challenges focused on the environment and sustainability. First up, in the Pattern Challenge, it’s another sewing bee first as the sewers are tasked with creating pants from old T-shirts. However, they are not asked to make just one pair - they have to make three. This challenge tests not only their technical skill but also their consistency. Then, Patrick and Esme take a trip to a store of waste destined for landfill to handpick the raw materials for the Transformation Challenge. Finally, the sewers get protesting as they make outfits with an environmental message made to measure their models.

Each part is sold on the black market, making it a potentially lucrative business for the criminals. Tracker Richard is racing to find a stolen Audi before it’s dismantled. According to the vehicle’s tracker, it’s being stored in a garage in Newport, south Wales. But will Richard get to it in time? At Felixstowe port, stolen vehicle examiner Adam discovers a shipping container crammed full of car parts. Adam’s job is to piece together the parts and identify the stolen vehicles, one by one. Caravans and motorhomes are also being targeted by criminal gangs. But one proud owner gave chase when his motorhome was stolen. Dramatic dashcam footage shows how he closed in on the thief, eventually forcing him to abandon the stolen motorhome at the side of the road and make his getaway on foot.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: After a teenager is found dead in the woods, a pathologist analyses her stab wounds to shed light on the attack. Plus, when remains are found in Scotland, a crack team of experts nail the killer.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A derelict cottage in Dorset has Martin debating whether it’s more viable to demolish and start again rather than refurbish. Dion’s in Yorkshire, where an end terrace has some structural issues, and in west London Owain loves the potential of a lower ground floor flat.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion hosts as the red and blue teams go head-to-head at Carmarthen Antiques and Flea Market in west Wales, with the expert help of Philip Serrell and Charles Hanson. Who will buy the most profitable three items to take to auction? Christina visits the nearby Gwili Steam Railway and finds out how it has been preserved for future generations.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: At Altrincham recycling centre, Jacqui stops three potential money-makers from being crushed. She enlists carpenter Ollie to overhaul a coffee table, but will his bonkers plan including concrete and a traffic cone prove to be a winner? For her own project, Jacqui tries to add a creative touch to a collection of old frames, but will the results be as pretty as a picture?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: North Yorkshire is calling, and Briony May Williams is on the case as she helps a London buyer and her beloved dog Buddy swap city bustle for a country cottage. With a £350,000 budget as well as her human best buddy by her side for support, the trio discover charming homes, towns and villages for this rural getaway. Briony also meets a family living on the edge of the amazing moors, where they now roast their own coffee beans for their thriving cafe.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: A widow needs help to sell her collectibles. JB finds a rare watch that could make a small fortune at auction, and Robin turns to toothpaste to help restore an antique.

programme.desc: The brainy quiz returns - but this time host Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Gyles Brandreth. As always, contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It’s week 3, and it's time for Reduce, Reuse, Recycle. Presenter Sophie Willan, alongside judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young, takes the fight to fast fashion with three challenges focused on the environment and sustainability. First up, in the Pattern Challenge, it’s another sewing bee first as the sewers are tasked with creating pants from old T-shirts. However, they are not asked to make just one pair - they have to make three. This challenge tests not only their technical skill but also their consistency. Then, Patrick and Esme take a trip to a store of waste destined for landfill to handpick the raw materials for the Transformation Challenge. Finally, the sewers get protesting as they make outfits with an environmental message made to measure their models.

programme.title: Blinded by the Light
programme.desc: Luton, 1987. Javed Khan is a British Pakistani college student in a family with a domineering father. Facing parental pressure and everyday racism, Javed unexpectedly finds his frustrations and ambitions expressed in Bruce Springsteen songs. Inspired by the rock star and a teacher who encourages his own writing, he sets out to fulfill his dreams. Feelgood drama with music, inspired by a true story.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: A dramatic new chapter begins at Longleat. After more than 50 years, hippos are returning to the park, but with hopes of creating a world-class breeding programme, the pressure is on. The team must race to finish a state-of-the-art hippo house in time while the keepers travel across Europe on a mission to learn everything they can about their precious new arrivals. But bringing together a pod of hippos who’ve never met and mixing them with the park’s sea lions could spell disaster. Elsewhere, Ben witnesses a rare moment as the Cuban crocodiles show a terrifying pack-hunting display, while on the other side of the park, the keepers hope for peace between the park’s battling hyenas after a savage attack. In Lion Country, Caleb uncovers the astonishingly clever tactics of an ageing lioness determined to outwit her pride and stay strong, and there’s heartstopping jeopardy as Megan helps reintroduce giant tortoises to the sunshine. Meanwhile, Hamza’s bird survey uncovers spectacular scenes in the skies above Half Mile Pond.

programme.desc: Many stolen cars end up in illegal garages known as chop shops, where they’re broken up for parts. Each part is sold on the black market, making it a potentially lucrative business for the criminals. Tracker Richard is racing to find a stolen Audi before it’s dismantled. According to the vehicle’s tracker, it’s being stored in a garage in Newport, south Wales. But will Richard get to it in time? At Felixstowe port, stolen vehicle examiner Adam discovers a shipping container crammed full of car parts. Adam’s job is to piece together the parts and identify the stolen vehicles, one by one. Caravans and motorhomes are also being targeted by criminal gangs. But one proud owner gave chase when his motorhome was stolen. Dramatic dashcam footage shows how he closed in on the thief, eventually forcing him to abandon the stolen motorhome at the side of the road and make his getaway on foot.

programme.title: The Bidding Room

All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It’s week 3, and it's time for Reduce, Reuse, Recycle. Presenter Sophie Willan, alongside judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young, takes the fight to fast fashion with three challenges focused on the environment and sustainability. First up, in the Pattern Challenge, it’s another sewing bee first as the sewers are tasked with creating pants from old T-shirts. However, they are not asked to make just one pair - they have to make three. This challenge tests not only their technical skill but also their consistency. Then, Patrick and Esme take a trip to a store of waste destined for landfill to handpick the raw materials for the Transformation Challenge. Finally, the sewers get protesting as they make outfits with an environmental message made to measure their models.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: A dramatic new chapter begins at Longleat. After more than 50 years, hippos are returning to the park, but with hopes of creating a world-class breeding programme, the pressure is on. The team must race to finish a state-of-the-art hippo house in time while the keepers travel across Europe on a mission to learn everything they can about their precious new arrivals. But bringing together a pod of hippos who’ve never met and mixing them with the park’s sea lions could spell disaster. Elsewhere, Ben witnesses a rare moment as the Cuban crocodiles show a terrifying pack-hunting display, while on the other side of the park, the keepers hope for peace between the park’s battling hyenas after a savage attack. In Lion Country, Caleb uncovers the astonishingly clever tactics of an ageing lioness determined to outwit her pride and stay strong, and there’s heartstopping jeopardy as Megan helps reintroduce giant tortoises to the sunshine. Meanwhile, Hamza’s bird survey uncovers spectacular scenes in the skies above Half Mile Pond.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: A dramatic new chapter begins at Longleat. After more than 50 years, hippos are returning to the park, but with hopes of creating a world-class breeding programme, the pressure is on. The team must race to finish a state-of-the-art hippo house in time while the keepers travel across Europe on a mission to learn everything they can about their precious new arrivals. But bringing together a pod of hippos who’ve never met and mixing them with the park’s sea lions could spell disaster. Elsewhere, Ben witnesses a rare moment as the Cuban crocodiles show a terrifying pack-hunting display, while on the other side of the park, the keepers hope for peace between the park’s battling hyenas after a savage attack. In Lion Country, Caleb uncovers the astonishingly clever tactics of an ageing lioness determined to outwit her pride and stay strong, and there’s heartstopping jeopardy as Megan helps reintroduce giant tortoises to the sunshine. Meanwhile, Hamza’s bird survey uncovers spectacular scenes in the skies above Half Mile Pond.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Many stolen cars end up in illegal garages known as chop shops, where they’re broken up for parts. Each part is sold on the black market, making it a potentially lucrative business for the criminals. Tracker Richard is racing to find a stolen Audi before it’s dismantled. According to the vehicle’s tracker, it’s being stored in a garage in Newport, south Wales. But will Richard get to it in time? At Felixstowe port, stolen vehicle examiner Adam discovers a shipping container crammed full of car parts. Adam’s job is to piece together the parts and identify the stolen vehicles, one by one. Caravans and motorhomes are also being targeted by criminal gangs. But one proud owner gave chase when his motorhome was stolen. Dramatic dashcam footage shows how he closed in on the thief, eventually forcing him to abandon the stolen motorhome at the side of the road and make his getaway on foot.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: After a teenager is found dead in the woods, a pathologist analyses her stab wounds to shed light on the attack. Plus, when remains are found in Scotland, a crack team of experts nail the killer.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A derelict cottage in Dorset has Martin debating whether it’s more viable to demolish and start again rather than refurbish. Dion’s in Yorkshire, where an end terrace has some structural issues, and in west London Owain loves the potential of a lower ground floor flat.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion hosts as the red and blue teams go head-to-head at Carmarthen Antiques and Flea Market in west Wales, with the expert help of Philip Serrell and Charles Hanson. Who will buy the most profitable three items to take to auction? Christina visits the nearby Gwili Steam Railway and finds out how it has been preserved for future generations.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: North Yorkshire is calling, and Briony May Williams is on the case as she helps a London buyer and her beloved dog Buddy swap city bustle for a country cottage. With a £350,000 budget as well as her human best buddy by her side for support, the trio discover charming homes, towns and villages for this rural getaway. Briony also meets a family living on the edge of the amazing moors, where they now roast their own coffee beans for their thriving cafe.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: A dramatic new chapter begins at Longleat. After more than 50 years, hippos are returning to the park, but with hopes of creating a world-class breeding programme, the pressure is on. The team must race to finish a state-of-the-art hippo house in time while the keepers travel across Europe on a mission to learn everything they can about their precious new arrivals. But bringing together a pod of hippos who’ve never met and mixing them with the park’s sea lions could spell disaster. Elsewhere, Ben witnesses a rare moment as the Cuban crocodiles show a terrifying pack-hunting display, while on the other side of the park, the keepers hope for peace between the park’s battling hyenas after a savage attack. In Lion Country, Caleb uncovers the astonishingly clever tactics of an ageing lioness determined to outwit her pride and stay strong, and there’s heartstopping jeopardy as Megan helps reintroduce giant tortoises to the sunshine. Meanwhile, Hamza’s bird survey uncovers spectacular scenes in the skies above Half Mile Pond.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Many stolen cars end up in illegal garages known as chop shops, where they’re broken up for parts. Each part is sold on the black market, making it a potentially lucrative business for the criminals. Tracker Richard is racing to find a stolen Audi before it’s dismantled. According to the vehicle’s tracker, it’s being stored in a garage in Newport, south Wales. But will Richard get to it in time? At Felixstowe port, stolen vehicle examiner Adam discovers a shipping container crammed full of car parts. Adam’s job is to piece together the parts and identify the stolen vehicles, one by one. Caravans and motorhomes are also being targeted by criminal gangs. But one proud owner gave chase when his motorhome was stolen. Dramatic dashcam footage shows how he closed in on the thief, eventually forcing him to abandon the stolen motorhome at the side of the road and make his getaway on foot.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: After a teenager is found dead in the woods, a pathologist analyses her stab wounds to shed light on the attack. Plus, when remains are found in Scotland, a crack team of experts nail the killer.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A derelict cottage in Dorset has Martin debating whether it’s more viable to demolish and start again rather than refurbish. Dion’s in Yorkshire, where an end terrace has some structural issues, and in west London Owain loves the potential of a lower ground floor flat.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion hosts as the red and blue teams go head-to-head at Carmarthen Antiques and Flea Market in west Wales, with the expert help of Philip Serrell and Charles Hanson. Who will buy the most profitable three items to take to auction? Christina visits the nearby Gwili Steam Railway and finds out how it has been preserved for future generations.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: At Altrincham recycling centre, Jacqui stops three potential money-makers from being crushed. She enlists carpenter Ollie to overhaul a coffee table, but will his bonkers plan including concrete and a traffic cone prove to be a winner? For her own project, Jacqui tries to add a creative touch to a collection of old frames, but will the results be as pretty as a picture?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: North Yorkshire is calling, and Briony May Williams is on the case as she helps a London buyer and her beloved dog Buddy swap city bustle for a country cottage. With a £350,000 budget as well as her human best buddy by her side for support, the trio discover charming homes, towns and villages for this rural getaway. Briony also meets a family living on the edge of the amazing moors, where they now roast their own coffee beans for their thriving cafe.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: A widow needs help to sell her collectibles. JB finds a rare watch that could make a small fortune at auction, and Robin turns to toothpaste to help restore an antique.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: The brainy quiz returns - but this time host Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Gyles Brandreth. As always, contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: Sheila is left shaken after a tense visit with Gray. Tensions continue to rise between George and Nicola.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It’s week 3, and it's time for Reduce, Reuse, Recycle. Presenter Sophie Willan, alongside judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young, takes the fight to fast fashion with three challenges focused on the environment and sustainability. First up, in the Pattern Challenge, it’s another sewing bee first as the sewers are tasked with creating pants from old T-shirts. However, they are not asked to make just one pair - they have to make three. This challenge tests not only their technical skill but also their consistency. Then, Patrick and Esme take a trip to a store of waste destined for landfill to handpick the raw materials for the Transformation Challenge. Finally, the sewers get protesting as they make outfits with an environmental message made to measure their models.

programme.title: Reporting Scotland
programme.desc: More from the day’s top stories and communities across Scotland.

programme.title: My Kind of Town
programme.desc: Ian and Major head to Wick, a royal burgh in Caithness. At one time a vast herring port, the town is now trying to maximise tourism from its location on the North Coast 500 route. Ian enjoys the stunning landscape while kayaking and admires some of the Iron Age remains for which the area is famous. Against his better judgement, he is also persuaded to take a chilly dip in an outdoor pool carved into the harbour.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: In Dumfries and Galloway, the Thomson family meet to discuss plans for Nick’s succession, but there has been a growing change of heart. Near Glasgow, the Imrie family prepare to co-host a gourmet dining event featuring their home-grown lamb, but a storm threatens proceedings. In Caithness, Sally takes her four-year-old to market to sell his first lambs along with 20 of her own, and Sally’s mum, Julie, comes home for a visit.

programme.title: The Beauty Queen and the Catfish
programme.desc: Dr David Graham is online and looking for love. He seems to have it all: the looks, the job, and the charisma. On paper, he’s Kilmarnock’s most eligible bachelor. But when the town’s former beauty queen Abbie Draper starts to receive messages from him after he treats her grandfather in hospital, she gets the feeling he might be too good to be true. She turns online sleuth and starts to uncover a trail of deception, crazy coincidences and stories that just don’t add up. Dr David isn’t just a bad boyfriend; something more sinister is afoot. Abbie starts trying to figure out who David Graham really is and why he is doing this.

programme.title: The Beauty Queen and the Catfish
programme.desc: Dr David’s victims begin comparing their stories, and it becomes clear they are dealing with a sophisticated catfish. But nothing could prepare them for the shocking truth of the perpetrator’s true identity, which leaves the women with more questions than answers. But when beauty queen Abbie takes these findings to the police, they are unable to do anything about it, and the Catfish of Kilmarnock remains free to target more and more victims. Abbie can’t walk away, and steps up her investigation over months that turn into years. As she continues to track the catfish, the scale of their criminality comes into focus, with victims spread across the country and dating back over a decade. This is one of the UK’s most prolific ever catfish, and they are not done yet.

programme.title: The Beauty Queen and the Catfish
programme.desc: As criminal investigations take hold, the victims finally have justice, but they are still left urgently searching for answers as they try to rebuild their lives. What drives someone, with a seemingly normal life, to throw it all away to terrorise countless women from the same town? With no clear motive and no explanation from the person in the frame, this very modern true crime tale now turns to those closest to the perpetrator, who are also trying to understand the mystery behind the repeated cycles of offending. As the beauty queen and the catfish’s lives become ever more entangled, lines begin to blur, loyalties are tested, and Abbie finds herself questioning everything as history repeats, and the moral complexity of crime and punishment in the internet age is laid bare. For the many victims, the question remains: what drives someone to become one of the UK’s most prolific catfish - and why can’t they stop?

programme.title: BBC New Comedy Awards
programme.desc: The BBC’s big comedy talent search heads north to Scotland and the iconic Paisley Town Hall, which, following a multi-million-pound revamp, has been transformed into a world-class venue and top performance spaces. Five acts take to the stage in front of a packed house of more than 200 comedy lovers. Award-winning Glaswegian stand-up comedian Larry Dean is our host for the evening and joining him are the three judges – writer, comedian and actor Ashley Storrie, who recently picked up two Bafta nominations for her BBC Three comedy, Dinosaur; and the writer of the multi-award-winning Scottish sitcom Two Doors Down, Gregor Sharp. Plus, our head judge, Babatunde Aleshe, is on hand to keep the house in order. Craig Scott, Maddy Fernando, Jonathan Oldfield, JoJo Maberly and Katie McLeod perform their set before the judges decide who will go through to the grand final in November.

programme.title: Small Town, Big Riot
programme.desc: Mobeen Azhar investigates how a protest outside an asylum seeker hotel turned into a riot, uncovering a blueprint for a national wave of violence that eight months later would affect us all.

programme.title: Small Town, Big Riot
programme.desc: Mobeen Azhar returns to Kirkby to try to connect the dots between a whirlwind of misinformation and growing unrest outside sites housing asylum seekers. He soon finds out that a local man with white supremacist views and connections was campaigning outside the Suites hotel in the run-up to the riot. The question is, how much did this influence what took place days later? With that man now serving time in prison for stirring up racial hatred, Mobeen’s investigation takes him further afield to a former RAF base called Scampton. Since the night of the riot in Kirkby, the policy of the then Conservative government shifted. They began shutting down asylum seeker hotels in favour of bigger sites like Scampton.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Naturalist Steve Backshall has travelled the world in search of animals for his Deadly 60 list. Many of the animals he has encountered are armed and highly dangerous. This programme looks back at some of Steve's favourite creatures, whose jaws, claws, venom and speed prove to be very useful weapons in the battle of the wild.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve Backshall and the Deadly 60 team travelled to six continents in search of animals for Steve's Deadly 60 list. They saw creatures with killer teeth, claws, jaws and venom. In fact they met so many incredible critters on their travels that they couldn't fit them all on the Deadly 60 list. Steve didn't want his audience to miss out, so he has given them their own programme.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Chris Harris and the £2m Bugatti Chiron attempt to cross the Arabian peninsula faster than Matt LeBlanc and a roster of money-no-object transport solutions. Back in Britain, Rory Reid constructs a life-size arcade game to test the Renault Twingo GT and its city car rivals, while rap star Tinie Tempah tackles the Top Gear track in the Reasonably Fast Toyota GT86.

programme.title: Shabaz Asks: Are Billionaires Bad?
programme.desc: After years of roasting the super-rich online, content creator and broadcaster Shabaz Ali comes face to face with a billionaire to see if they're as bad as everyone thinks.

programme.title: Good Bad Billionaire
programme.desc: How did the richest people on the planet make their billions? Beyoncé started out as a little girl competing in local talent shows, but over the course of a 30-year career in music, she transformed herself into a mogul worth $1 billion. Journalist Zing Tsjeng and BBC business editor Simon Jack trace Beyoncé’s early years in girl group Girls Tyme, the turbulent rise of Destiny’s Child and her breakout as a solo artist, before examining the strategic decisions that transformed her from performer to powerful businesswoman and entrepreneur. Beyonce’s rise to billionaire features conflicts with family and friends, brand battles, and questions around feminism, capitalism and control. Is she a force for empowerment, a ruthless operator or simply one of the most effective wealth builders in modern entertainment?

programme.title: Good Bad Billionaire
programme.desc: Cristiano Ronaldo grew up in poverty on the remote island of Madeira but became the first football player billionaire and one of the most recognisable people on the planet. BBC business editor Simon Jack and journalist Zing Tsjeng trace Ronaldo's rise from a homesick kid playing for the academy at Sporting CP to global superstardom at Manchester United and Real Madrid, where relentless training and record-breaking performances turned him into a sporting and commercial machine. Zing and Simon explore the business of modern football: from mega transfers and billion-dollar brand deals to tax battles and legal disputes. Ronaldo leveraged social media fame to build his CR7 empire, so is he the ultimate self-made success story, a divisive global brand or simply the most effective monetiser of talent in sporting history?

programme.title: Good Bad Billionaire
programme.desc: Jimmy Donaldson, better known as MrBeast, transformed himself from a teenager obsessing over YouTube's algorithms, into one of the most influential digital entrepreneurs on the planet. BBC business editor Simon Jack and journalist Zing Tsjeng follow his ascent from making Minecraft videos in his bedroom to ever-larger challenges, eye-watering cash prizes and headline-grabbing acts of philanthropy. Is MrBeast a visionary entrepreneur who reinvented entertainment for the internet generation, or has he simply mastered the art of turning clicks into cash? Good Bad Billionaire is the podcast that explores the lives of the super-rich and famous, tracking their wealth, philanthropy, business ethics and success. There are leaders who made their money in Silicon Valley, on Wall Street and in high-street fashion. From iconic celebrities and CEOs to titans of technology, the podcast unravels tales of fortune, power, economics, ambition and moral responsibility. Simon and Zing put their subjects to the test with a playful, totally unscientific scorecard - then hand the verdict over to you: are they good, bad or simply billionaires?

programme.title: The Tech Billionaire Takeover
programme.desc: A new generation of tech billionaires believe their technologies can replace democracy as we know it and upend the global financial system. Matt Shea gets inside access to this new super-elite, visiting the sovereign nations they're building and tracing their growing political connections to the Trump administration. Are these men trying to take over the world?

programme.title: Bergerac
programme.desc: Bergerac is a broken man, battling his demons and on leave after the death of his wife. But when a member of the Wakefields, one of Jersey’s wealthiest families, is murdered, chief of police Uma Dalal wants their best detective on the case. The Wakefields, led by patriarch Arthur, are keeping their cards close to their chests, whilst a man from Bergerac’s past surfaces to make a shocking accusation. Is Bergerac up to the job?

programme.title: Lifeline
programme.desc: Eddie Marsan presents this month’s Lifeline appeal on behalf of Tourettes Action, a charity which provides support, information and advocacy to improve the lives of people living with Tourette syndrome and their families.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Charlie Ross remembers a remarkable group of Second World War airmen who suffered life-changing injuries but refused to let those traumatic setbacks define them. In East Grinstead, Charlie learns about the Guinea Pig Club and the pioneering plastic surgeon who treated their physical and mental injuries. Nearby, two teams of bargain hunters race around the stalls of Ardingly antiques fair looking for collectable items they can sell at auction. In red are married couple Phil and Chris, who are looking for militaria, treen and anything quirky. Their opponents in blue are friends Abi and Emily, who have shiny and sparkly on their shopping list. With antiques expert Jonathan Pratt by their side, the reds weigh up a set of brass and wrought iron scales, which appeal to former blacksmith Phil. Across the fair, expert Kate Bliss shows the blues a 19th-century Tunbridge ware box, but it’s not an open and shut case for Abi. For the sale, the teams travel to Buckinghamshire, where Hugo Lemon gives his auctioneer estimates on their purchases, and for one duo, their bonus buy is definitely worth writing home about.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Kate Humble and Ben Fogle celebrate 25 years together on Animal Park, looking back at some of the animals, keepers and unforgettable moments they have shared, while new stories continue to unfold across the park. Young sea lion Rocky takes the biggest step of his life as he leaves the safety of his training area and joins the rest of the colony out on Half Mile Pond. As he finds his place alongside the adult sea lions and the park's newly arrived hippos, the keepers hope months of training will help him adapt to life in the open water. As part of the anniversary celebrations, Ben revisits the remarkable story of the park's Amur tiger cubs as Ginger and Seeka prepare to leave for new homes, while the team also celebrates 60 years since the safari park first opened its gates, transforming the way people experienced wildlife in Britain. Elsewhere, Megan meets the park's new hippos, Jon devises a new feeding challenge for the Cuban crocodiles, and the lionesses enjoy a very special birthday celebration.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It’s week 2, and judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young put the 11 remaining sewers through their paces with three challenges themed around prints and colours. First, the sewers take on the Pattern Challenge, constructing a pattern-matched shell top with adaptive elements, including invisible side-zips and a high-low hem. In the Transformation Challenge, they are given second-hand clothes in purple and brown, the judges’ least-favourite colours, and have to create garments that will convince them to change their minds. Finally, in the Made-to-Measure, the sewers must create an eye-catching outfit in just one colour.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week the celebrity contestants Yasmine Akram, Cariad Lloyd, Geoff Norcott and Dennis Taylor take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quick-fire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games kitchen composter?

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and his sidekick Sarah Greene host this quiz show where the contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple - make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Hairy Bikers' Bakeation
programme.desc: The second leg of the Hairy Bikers' Bakeation begins on the flatlands of the Netherlands where they bake lazybones buns beside a windmill and discover that the Netherlands baking tradition reflects the country's past as a nation at the heart of the spice trade. This is particularly true of the classic Dutch apple pie, smothered in cinnamon and some traditional Jewish buns coated in muscovado sugar. Their next port of call is Belgium, where they cook up an indulgent Belgian chocolate truffle cheesecake but not before they have tasted the chocolate delights of Bruges, including chocolate tequila cocktails. In front of the Atomium and surrounded by curious Chinese tourists, they rustle up a mouth-watering pork pie with Riesling jelly. The third country on this leg of their trip is Luxembourg. Along the way they meet some real characters; Michelin-starred chef Lea makes macaroons with ice cream on top; Harry bakes traditional sweet buns but his real passion is VW campervans and a shock-o-latier (chocolatier), Dominique, invites them to snort chocolate powder using a device invented for the Rolling Stones.

programme.title: The Farmers' Country Showdown
programme.desc: Friends Neil and Kai started their chilli farm in 2019 and now grow over 500 pesticide-free plants in their Wye Valley polytunnels. As they are a young business, taking their products to the prestigious Abergavenny Food Festival for the first time is a big deal for them. Hoping to turn customers’ heads with their fresh chillies and flavoured salts, they’re also launching their new chilli ice creams to the public. Over in the Monnow Valley, Kevin is bottling up his award-winning Welsh cider, perry and apple juice. He and his partner Natalie are passionate about managing orchards in a wildlife-friendly way. For both these small-scale farming businesses, if sales go well on the day, the festival will be a great financial boost.

programme.title: Earth from Space
programme.desc: Cameras in space tell stories of life on our planet from a brand new perspective. Earth’s surface is covered in weird and wonderful patterns. The Australian outback is covered in pale spots, the work of wombats; a clearing in the endless green canopy of the Congo rainforest has been created by an incredible elephant gathering; and the twists and turns of the Amazon make a home for rehabilitated manatees. This is our home, as we’ve never seen it before.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin presents from Lulworth Castle in Dorset. Antiques experts Catherine Southon and Mark Stacey find the best antiques and collectables to take to auction. Paul also explores the turbulent history of the Weld family and their struggles against Catholic persecution over 300 years.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Karen Hauer, Storm Huntley, Joe Marler and Tom Read Wilson take on a series of rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games suitcase, or will they be tempted with the House of Games bee hotel?

programme.title: Just One Thing
programme.desc: In Brighton, Zoe Ball wants to help retired woodworker Neville get his health back on track after a series of heart attacks. Her prescription is delightfully simple: Neville should add a little sunshine into his life. Just ten minutes of sunlight a day has been shown to improve heart health, strengthen bones and lift your mood. A small dose of daylight could make a big difference.

programme.title: Rick Stein’s Food Stories
programme.desc: In the Lake District, Rick meets Kevin Tickle, a chef who loves to forage, and the sheep farmer and author James Rebanks. He visits an old friend in Morecambe Bay with a secret recipe for the best potted shrimps. In Yorkshire, he discovers the story of yorkshire pudding and visits the UK’s biggest tofu factory. He cooks tofu pad thai, aubergine biryani and, with his son Jack, makes his mum’s shepherd’s pie.

programme.title: Amazing Hotels: Life Beyond the Lobby
programme.desc: Rob Rinder and Monica Galetti work at Six Senses Ibiza on the island’s north coast. They help guests in the hotel’s on-site clinic experience biohacking therapies, from cryotherapy to heated infrared masks, promising to delay ageing and increase vitality. Rob helps the hotel’s 'energy balancing' expert create a cacao ceremony to increase spiritual wellness. In the basement, Monica uncovers a recording studio with a party space for the music scene that the island is known for.

programme.title: Interview with the Vampire
programme.desc: The switch from recluse to rock star begins Lestat’s tell-all recordings, leading to a brutal hotel confrontation. But global turmoil lies ahead.

programme.title: Live at the Apollo
programme.desc: The critically-acclaimed Jamali Maddix introduces the impressive comedy talents of rising stars Fern Brady and Sindhu Vee to the stage.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: The New Boy
programme.desc: In the Australian outback in the mid-1940s, a young orphan is brought to a remote orphanage run by two nuns. As he is struggling to fit in, the boy's presence begins to disturb those around him.

programme.title: Natalie Cassidy: Caring Together
programme.desc: Natalie experiences what it's like to have dementia and puts her learning into practice on a very special placement.

programme.title: Bergerac
programme.desc: Bergerac is a broken man, battling his demons and on leave after the death of his wife. But when a member of the Wakefields, one of Jersey’s wealthiest families, is murdered, chief of police Uma Dalal wants their best detective on the case. The Wakefields, led by patriarch Arthur, are keeping their cards close to their chests, whilst a man from Bergerac’s past surfaces to make a shocking accusation. Is Bergerac up to the job?

programme.title: Lifeline
programme.desc: Eddie Marsan presents this month’s Lifeline appeal on behalf of Tourettes Action, a charity which provides support, information and advocacy to improve the lives of people living with Tourette syndrome and their families.

With antiques expert Jonathan Pratt by their side, the reds weigh up a set of brass and wrought iron scales, which appeal to former blacksmith Phil. Across the fair, expert Kate Bliss shows the blues a 19th-century Tunbridge ware box, but it’s not an open and shut case for Abi. For the sale, the teams travel to Buckinghamshire, where Hugo Lemon gives his auctioneer estimates on their purchases, and for one duo, their bonus buy is definitely worth writing home about.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Kate Humble and Ben Fogle celebrate 25 years together on Animal Park, looking back at some of the animals, keepers and unforgettable moments they have shared, while new stories continue to unfold across the park. Young sea lion Rocky takes the biggest step of his life as he leaves the safety of his training area and joins the rest of the colony out on Half Mile Pond. As he finds his place alongside the adult sea lions and the park's newly arrived hippos, the keepers hope months of training will help him adapt to life in the open water. As part of the anniversary celebrations, Ben revisits the remarkable story of the park's Amur tiger cubs as Ginger and Seeka prepare to leave for new homes, while the team also celebrates 60 years since the safari park first opened its gates, transforming the way people experienced wildlife in Britain. Elsewhere, Megan meets the park's new hippos, Jon devises a new feeding challenge for the Cuban crocodiles, and the lionesses enjoy a very special birthday celebration.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It’s week 2, and judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young put the 11 remaining sewers through their paces with three challenges themed around prints and colours. First, the sewers take on the Pattern Challenge, constructing a pattern-matched shell top with adaptive elements, including invisible side-zips and a high-low hem. In the Transformation Challenge, they are given second-hand clothes in purple and brown, the judges’ least-favourite colours, and have to create garments that will convince them to change their minds. Finally, in the Made-to-Measure, the sewers must create an eye-catching outfit in just one colour.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week the celebrity contestants Yasmine Akram, Cariad Lloyd, Geoff Norcott and Dennis Taylor take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quick-fire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games kitchen composter?

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and his sidekick Sarah Greene host this quiz show where the contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple - make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Hairy Bikers' Bakeation
programme.desc: The second leg of the Hairy Bikers' Bakeation begins on the flatlands of the Netherlands where they bake lazybones buns beside a windmill and discover that the Netherlands baking tradition reflects the country's past as a nation at the heart of the spice trade. This is particularly true of the classic Dutch apple pie, smothered in cinnamon and some traditional Jewish buns coated in muscovado sugar. Their next port of call is Belgium, where they cook up an indulgent Belgian chocolate truffle cheesecake but not before they have tasted the chocolate delights of Bruges, including chocolate tequila cocktails. In front of the Atomium and surrounded by curious Chinese tourists, they rustle up a mouth-watering pork pie with Riesling jelly. The third country on this leg of their trip is Luxembourg. Along the way they meet some real characters; Michelin-starred chef Lea makes macaroons with ice cream on top; Harry bakes traditional sweet buns but his real passion is VW campervans and a shock-o-latier (chocolatier), Dominique, invites them to snort chocolate powder using a device invented for the Rolling Stones.

programme.title: The Farmers' Country Showdown
programme.desc: Friends Neil and Kai started their chilli farm in 2019 and now grow over 500 pesticide-free plants in their Wye Valley polytunnels. As they are a young business, taking their products to the prestigious Abergavenny Food Festival for the first time is a big deal for them. Hoping to turn customers’ heads with their fresh chillies and flavoured salts, they’re also launching their new chilli ice creams to the public. Over in the Monnow Valley, Kevin is bottling up his award-winning Welsh cider, perry and apple juice. He and his partner Natalie are passionate about managing orchards in a wildlife-friendly way. For both these small-scale farming businesses, if sales go well on the day, the festival will be a great financial boost.

programme.title: Earth from Space
programme.desc: Cameras in space tell stories of life on our planet from a brand new perspective. Earth’s surface is covered in weird and wonderful patterns. The Australian outback is covered in pale spots, the work of wombats; a clearing in the endless green canopy of the Congo rainforest has been created by an incredible elephant gathering; and the twists and turns of the Amazon make a home for rehabilitated manatees. This is our home, as we’ve never seen it before.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin presents from Lulworth Castle in Dorset. Antiques experts Catherine Southon and Mark Stacey find the best antiques and collectables to take to auction. Paul also explores the turbulent history of the Weld family and their struggles against Catholic persecution over 300 years.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Karen Hauer, Storm Huntley, Joe Marler and Tom Read Wilson take on a series of rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. programme.title: Just One Thing
programme.desc: In Brighton, Zoe Ball wants to help retired woodworker Neville get his health back on track after a series of heart attacks. Her prescription is delightfully simple: Neville should add a little sunshine into his life. Just ten minutes of sunlight a day has been shown to improve heart health, strengthen bones and lift your mood. A small dose of daylight could make a big difference.

programme.title: Rick Stein’s Food Stories
programme.desc: In the Lake District, Rick meets Kevin Tickle, a chef who loves to forage, and the sheep farmer and author James Rebanks. He visits an old friend in Morecambe Bay with a secret recipe for the best potted shrimps. In Yorkshire, he discovers the story of yorkshire pudding and visits the UK’s biggest tofu factory. He cooks tofu pad thai, aubergine biryani and, with his son Jack, makes his mum’s shepherd’s pie.

programme.title: Amazing Hotels: Life Beyond the Lobby
programme.desc: Rob Rinder and Monica Galetti work at Six Senses Ibiza on the island’s north coast. They help guests in the hotel’s on-site clinic experience biohacking therapies, from cryotherapy to heated infrared masks, promising to delay ageing and increase vitality. Rob helps the hotel’s 'energy balancing' expert create a cacao ceremony to increase spiritual wellness. In the basement, Monica uncovers a recording studio with a party space for the music scene that the island is known for.

programme.title: Interview with the Vampire
programme.desc: The switch from recluse to rock star begins Lestat’s tell-all recordings, leading to a brutal hotel confrontation. But global turmoil lies ahead.

programme.title: If Walls Could Talk
programme.desc: From the stories on the front page to those behind the scenes, well-known local journalists like Alf McCreary, John Laverty and Ivan Little take us on a journey through their years spent within the walls of the Telegraph building until the paper moved out. Young local DJs reveal its current popularity as one of the most sought-after music venues in the city.

programme.title: The Band

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops

programme.title: Hey Duggee

Tino starts to float up into the sky! He's having a rather good time, until he gets stuck in a tree. It's time for the Squirrels to come to his rescue.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Duggee and the Squirrels decide to play hide-and-seek. Duggee counts to ten while the Squirrels go off and hide. They have hidden in really good places, but Duggee finds them all - except Roly. He's not in the tent. He's not in the clubhouse. He doesn't seem to be anywhere outside. Where could he be? Maybe the cows have seen where Roly is hiding.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Dad agrees to take Bluey and Bingo to buy an ice cream if they can get him into the car.

programme.title: Bluey
